paragraphs: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde has unveiled ten shortlisted design concepts for future euro banknotes, selected from over 1,200 proposals.

The designs represent two main themes chosen to reflect European identity. The first theme focuses on prominent cultural figures in history, including artist Leonardo da Vinci, opera singer Maria Callas, scientist Marie Curie, and composer Ludwig van Beethoven. The second theme highlights nature and depicts various European bird species in river landscapes alongside major European Union institutions to emphasize Europe’s biodiversity and environmental protection.

For the first time, European citizens will participate in selecting the final theme through an online survey hosted on the central bank’s website. Following the public vote and final design selection, technical preparation and production stages will begin. The new banknotes, which will be worth from 5 to 500 euros, are expected to enter circulation starting from the end of 2026.

paragraphs: The European Central Bank has shown ten finalist designs for new euro cash notes. Over 1,200 ideas were sent in, but leaders chose two big ideas to show European culture and nature.

The first idea features famous historic leaders in art, science, and music, such as Leonardo da Vinci, Maria Callas, Marie Curie, and Beethoven. The second idea features wild birds and beautiful rivers, and shows the need to protect nature and animals across Europe.

People living in the EU can vote for their favorite idea in an online survey on the bank’s website. After the vote, the central bank will start printing the new paper money. People are expected to start using these new euro notes from the end of 2026.
